applies_to: decimal(p,s) with s <= 10 -> DECIMAL(p,s), and any decimal port computed under 'Enable high precision = NO'; bind per field in the mapping spec, never to a port with s > 10
why: Informatica ROUND rounds half away from zero and high-precision-off sessions compute decimals in double (15 significant digits); places 10 neutralises sub-1e-10 double noise while last-digit errors at any scale <= 10 still fail Tier 3. The harness holds one params set per rule name, so a port with s > 10 gets `identity` (raw compare) until per-field `places` exists (harness gap). Tighten per unit only under a recorded decision.

applies_to: date/time ports fed by SYSDATE / SESSSTARTTIME / SYSTIMESTAMP('NS'), ports written under 'Pre 85 Timestamp Compatibility', and zoned timestamps -> TIMESTAMP_NTZ, TIMESTAMP; bind per field, never to a pass-through TIMESTAMP(6) column
why: Only those columns legitimately differ below the millisecond (nanosecond clock reads, pre-8.5 second precision, zone normalisation to UTC). Teradata/Oracle TIMESTAMP(6) values are carried at microseconds by both engines and Delta, so they compare with `identity` and a sub-millisecond mismatch stays a Tier 3 failure.

CHAR-origin ports (Teradata, DB2, mainframe) and fixed-width flat files with STRIPTRAILINGBLANKS=NO deliver padded strings; IS_SPACES ports become '' after trimming. Evaluate IS_SPACES/LENGTH on the untrimmed value in converted code.

Flat-file NULL_CHARACTER, Oracle targets folding '' to NULL (fixture ORA_MDM_HUB_PROD), REG_EXTRACT no-match ('' in Spark, NULL in Informatica) and two-argument IIF returning ''. Whether '' and NULL compare equal is the STOP A policy.
Unconnected output ports and unmatched lookup ports are NULL on the legacy side while the converted keyed-diff document may omit the column.

params.enabled_if: case-insensitive compare flags found in census (REPLACESTR/REPLACECHR/IN caseFlag 0, Lookup/Joiner 'Case Sensitive String Comparison = NO', Sorter 'Case Sensitive = NO')

why: Only for columns whose legacy comparison was case-insensitive; Informatica string comparison is case-sensitive by default, so this rule is never bound globally.
Explicit no-op for fields that must compare raw. Sequence Generator surrogate keys are excluded from Tier 3 rather than canonicalised.
